definition: In photography and computer vision, an omnidirectional camera (from "omni", meaning all), also known as 360-degree camera (or 360° camera), is a camera having a field of view that covers at least a full circle (360°) in the horizontal plane.
details: It may be extended vertically up to a full sphere (1 spat), in which case it is also known as a spherical camera. Omnidirectional cameras are important in applications where large visual field coverage is needed, such as in panoramic photography, VR photography, and robotics.

explainer.lead: An omnidirectional camera, also called a 360-degree camera, has a field of view covering at least a full circle (360°) in the horizontal plane. It matters where large visual coverage is needed.

tiers.eli5: Like standing in one spot and seeing everything around you at once instead of just what's in front.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on it for panoramic and VR photography and for robotics, where wide coverage replaces or supplements panning cameras. Vertical coverage may extend to a full sphere, in which case it is a spherical camera.
tiers.paperLevel: Field of view covers at least 360° horizontally; vertically it may extend to a full sphere (1 spat), making it a spherical camera.

explainer.example: A robot fitted with an omnidirectional camera captures a full horizontal view of its surroundings in a single frame.
